item.title: Alex de Minaur's Relentless Rise: The Demon Within Tennis
item.description:
Alex de Minaur’s Relentless Rise: The Demon Within Tennis

What does it take to climb back into the world’s top six after an injury-ravaged season? Just ask Alex de Minaur, the Australian dynamo whose nickname “The Demon” feels more earned with every match. While headlines obsess over Sinner and Alcaraz, de Minaur keeps quietly stacking titles, defying expectations, and forcing the tennis world to take him seriously.

Quick Summary: Alex de Minaur has battled back from a hip injury and a brutal 2025 season to reclaim World No. 6, winning the Rotterdam Open by defeating Felix Auger-Aliassime in straight sets. Yet his French Open exit to Jakub Mensik reignited debates about whether his physical, attritional game can carry him to a Grand Slam breakthrough.

item.title: Jannik Sinner's Stunning 18-Match Streak Reshapes Tennis
item.description:
What if the best tennis player on the planet refused to call himself a defender? Jannik Sinner, the 24-year-old Italian world No. 1, just stretched his win streak to 18 matches in Madrid — and he says he is not protecting anything. He is “always chasing.”

Key Takeaways

  • Sinner has extended his current run to 18 straight wins at the 2026 Madrid Open.
  • He is hunting a fifth consecutive ATP Masters 1000 title while Carlos Alcaraz is sidelined.
  • Alcaraz withdrew from both the Italian Open and Roland Garros with a wrist injury.
  • Sinner and Alcaraz have split every major title of 2026 so far.
  • The Italian is reframing pressure: not defending, just chasing.

The numbers are staggering, but the story behind them is even better. Let’s break down why Sinner’s 2026 surge matters — and what it means for the rest of the tour.
